newsitem.title: INDIA: India cotton prices firm, new exports seen helping.
newsitem.headline: India cotton prices firm, new exports seen helping.

text.p: Indian cotton prices were steady in narrow trade on Thursday with mill demand low, dealers said.

New crop arrivals were low but are seen rising next week. In spot deals Bengal-deshi was steady at 915/940 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned was quiet at 1,590/1,680. Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) remained steady at 18,800/19,800 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).

"The government has allowed export of 15,000 tonnes of cotton yarn for November," said Chandulal Thakkar, a leading dealer. "This will boost export of yarn and will in turn boost demand for cotton by the mill owners," he added.
